newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Troops, police block party parades in Jakarta.
newsitem.headline: Troops, police block party parades in Jakarta.

text.p: Indonesian troops and riot police blocked thousands of supporters of a minority Moslem party from parading illegally on major Jakarta roads on Tuesday as the country's general election campaign gathered momentum.

Efforts by supporters of the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) to stage motorcycle and car parades caused traffic chaos in the teeming capital but there were no reports of violence or arrests.

The PPP, the ruling Golkar and the Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) are the only three parties legally permitted to contest polls for the 425 elected seats in the House of Representatives on May 29.
The other 75 seats are allotted to the military, which does not vote.
The parties agreed to campaign in different areas of the country each day, and the government banned street parades and marches to prevent violence between political partisans.
PPP Chairman Ismail Hasan Metareum, addressing a rally in Pasaruan in East Java that party officials said was attended by more than 100,000 people, defended the PPP's record in parliament.
"The PPP has opposed all things forbidden by religion, such as the state lottery and alcohol, and moreover PPP members in the Pasuran local parliament have succesfully opposed prostitution," he said.
"Also we have opposed and changed the contents of bills which were at odds with religion, especially Islam," he added.
Lieutenant-Colonel Syaiful Bakrie, head of Pasuruan police, told Reuters he estimated that around 50,000 people had attended the speech.
He added: "There were no problems, everything was safe."
The PPP campaigned on Tuesday on the main island of Java and in the remote Maluku islands and Irian Jaya in the east.

Golkar, seeking to push its share of votes above 70 percent after winning 68 percent in 1992, campaigned in Kalimantan on Borneo islands and Sulawesi, while the PDI took its case to Sumatra, the resort island of Bali and adjacent Nusa Nenggara islands.
The parties are seeking the support of nearly 125 million voters in the archipelago of more than 17,000 islands sprawling 5,000 km (3,000 miles) along the equator.

A split in the PDI after the ouster last year of party chief Megawati Sukarnoputri by government-backed rebels led to the first real violence of the campaign in the country's second city of Surabaya on Monday.

Witnesses said a rally by the official wing of the PDI was abandoned after Megawati supporters attacked the speakers' stage. There were no reports of injuries and security authorities dispersed the crowd.
The official PDI leader in Surabaya, Bachtiar Balukh, said however that the party might halt campaigning in the city as a result of the incident.
The incident was widely reported in the local press, but was shrugged off by financial markets, which had suffered an attack of nerves before the campaign started on Sunday.
The rupiah was virtually unchanged on the day, reaching a high of 2,422.75 after opening at 2,426.75 before settling at 2,426.50 by late afternoon.
The stock market was off nearly 9.30 points, or 1.42 percent, at 647.23, but brokers attributed this to suspension of an active stock and heavy profit-taking.
